Class ItemRenderOverrides

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.server.packs.resources.SimplePreparableReloadListener<Map<net.minecraft.resources.Identifier, ItemRenderConfig>>
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.client.ItemRenderOverrides
All Implemented Interfaces:
net.minecraft.server.packs.resources.PreparableReloadListener
public class ItemRenderOverrides extends net.minecraft.server.packs.resources.SimplePreparableReloadListener<Map<net.minecraft.resources.Identifier, ItemRenderConfig>>
The client's item render configuration, layered by authority. The first matching entry owns the entire presentation: the user's override file, then bundled resource overrides. Items absent from every layer use measured profiles.

A bundled resource-override file is named for the namespace whose items it covers, and covers no other. The bundled data spans mods, most of which any one client cannot use, so a file naming a namespace this client does not have is skipped without parsing or retention. A file whose name is not a namespace therefore applies to nothing.

    • resolve

      @Nullable public static RenderProfile resolve(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Resolves the item's presentation through the override layers. The first layer with an entry owns the presentation: only a missing mode is measured, because scale and offset mean different things from one mode to the next; missing scale and offset take plain defaults.
      Returns:
      the complete profile, or null for an empty stack.

    • handleWriteRequest

      public static void handleWriteRequest()
      Writes the user layer to the user override file and reports the result to the player. The map contains only entries the user explicitly set, so the file never accumulates measured or bundled values, and reset entries disappear from it.

    • handleDumpRequest

      public static void handleDumpRequest(List<String> namespaces)
      Dumps the resolved presentation of every item in these namespaces, one file per namespace under generated_overrides, and reports the result to the player. Entries are complete. The generated directory is output only, not an active override layer, so dumping a modpack does not freeze its current profiles into the user layer. Each file can be edited and copied into a resource pack's item_render_overrides.

      Every item a layer does not configure is measured here rather than at first sight of it, so a dump of a large pack is the measurement pass for all of it. The results reach the measured cache, which is saved once the dump is done rather than waiting for logout.
